einzeiler: Exploring the midlife pull toward religion through psychology, neuroscience, and Eastern…
kurzfassung: Arthur Brooks explores why many adults experience a growing urge toward spirituality and religion in midlife. Drawing on Hindu philosophy, specifically the four life stages known as ashramas, he examines how natural shifts in human intelligence drive this pursuit of deeper meaning. Finally, he offers practical steps for navigating this spiritual awakening without feeling bound by past identities.
stichpunkte: Many people in their thirties, forties, and fifties experience an unexpected urge to explore faith and spirituality.
Arthur Brooks shares his personal background growing up in an evangelical family and later converting to Catholicism.
Studying North Indian classical music and reading Hindu philosophy introduced Brooks to the Vedic concept of life's four quarters, called ashramas.
The Hindu framework outlines four life stages: student, householder, forest dweller, and the stage of enlightenment.
Midlife burnout often aligns with the transition from fluid intelligence to crystallized intelligence, prompting a search for deeper purpose.
The third life stage, vanaprastha, represents a metaphorical retirement into the forest focused on elite spiritual training and deeper wisdom.
Practical steps for this transition include softening current non-religious commitments, treating the journey as an entrepreneurial endeavor, and engaging in physical pilgrimages.

clips.hook: Hinduism's late arrival in the West
clips.text: Despite being an ancient tradition spanning thousands of years, Hinduism took a surprisingly long time to spread beyond the Indian subcontinent and influence Western culture.

clips.hook: Life expectancies in America and India
clips.text: Comparing average life spans reveals that Americans live to eighty-two on average, whereas the typical life expectancy in India reaches seventy-two years.

clips.hook: The endless cycle of the hedonic treadmill
clips.text: Billionaires often experience a sense of emptiness after earning their first massive fortune, leading them to chase yet another billion in a never-ending pursuit of satisfaction.

clips.hook: The massive surge of the non-religious
clips.text: While very few people identified as having no religious affiliation in the past, today roughly one-third of the population chooses this label.

clips.hook: Human stamina as an evolutionary hunting tool
clips.text: Early human predators possessed the remarkable endurance to exhaust and hunt swift prey solely by walking long distances without stopping.

beschreibung:
Why do so many people drift from faith in early adulthood, only to feel drawn back to it later in life?
In this episode of Office Hours, I explore the Hindu concept of Ashramas and the parallels with what modern science tells us about how our priorities change with age.
As we get older, the worldly rewards we once chased can start to feel less satisfying. We begin asking deeper questions about wisdom, meaning, and transcendence. That’s what happens when you enter Vanaprastha—the stage of life when we turn our attention inward.
I also share five practical steps for beginning (or rebeginning) your own spiritual journey.
